examples.en: I felt bad hearing such a half-hearted answer.
The staff member gave careless directions, so I got lost.

examples.ko: 숙제를 무성의하게 해 오면 선생님이 바로 알아요.
examples.en: If you do your homework carelessly, the teacher notices right away.
Customers can feel a half-hearted attitude right away.
The reply was so perfunctory that I was disappointed.
I complained about the service that was careless from start to finish.

explain: 주로 '무성의한 태도', '무성의하게 하다'처럼 형용사나 부사 형태로 써요. 일상에서는 '성의가 없다'라고도 많이 말하고, 반대는 '성의가 있다'예요.

phrases.example: 무성의한 태도로 손님을 대하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not treat customers with an insincere attitude.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-한'을 붙여 명사 앞에서 써요. 정성 없이 대하는 모습을 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-한' it goes before a noun, used to criticize a lack of care.

phrases.en: He answered the question without any effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-하게'가 동사를 꾸며서 대충, 정성 없이 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-하게' modifies a verb, meaning doing something carelessly and without effort.

phrases.en: This letter looks like it was written without sincerity.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무성의하다'를 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say '무성의하다'.

explain_en: It is mostly used in adjective or adverb form, as in '무성의한 태도' or '무성의하게 하다'. In daily talk people also say '성의가 없다', and the opposite is '성의가 있다'.

examples.en: The market was crowded and bustling with people.
The family lived together in a cramped little house.

examples.ko: 명절 전날 부엌에서 복작복작 음식을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The day before the holiday, we bustled about making food in the kitchen.
The kids are gathered in a crowd, playing.
There is a joy in living together crowded as a family.
It was a bustling mess inside the restaurant.

explain: 사람이 많이 모여 어수선하게 움직이는 모습을 나타내는 부사예요. 일상에서는 '북적북적'도 자주 써요. 뒤에 '붐비다, 모이다, 살다'처럼 사람이 있는 동작이 와요.

phrases.en: The street is bustling because of the festival.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning and more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: It's lunchtime, so the restaurant is bustling.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '하다' makes it describe a state.

phrases.en: The children are crowded together in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모이다'와 함께 쓰면 사람이 좁게 모인 모습이 잘 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '모이다', it shows people packed closely together.

explain_en: This adverb shows many people gathered and moving around busily. In daily speech '북적북적' is also common. It is followed by verbs about people such as '붐비다', '모이다' and '살다'.

examples.en: It turned out like this because of my carelessness.
It's all my fault. I'm really sorry.

examples.ko: 확인을 안 한 것은 담당자의 불찰이라고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think failing to check was the person in charge's oversight.

examples.ko: 이번 사고는 관리자의 불찰 때문에 일어났어요.
examples.en: This accident happened because of the manager's negligence.

examples.ko: 중요한 메일을 못 본 건 제 불찰이었어요.
examples.en: Missing the important email was my oversight.

examples.ko: 불찰을 인정하고 바로 사과하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to admit your oversight and apologize right away.

explain: 내 실수나 부주의를 인정하면서 정중히 말할 때 써요. 보통 '제 불찰이에요', '저의 불찰입니다'처럼 자기 잘못에 쓰고, 남에게 '네 불찰이야'라고 하면 차갑게 들려요. '실수'보다 격식 있어서 사과나 공식 발표에 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: The company admitted its lapse in management.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 실수나 부주의를 공식적으로 받아들인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means officially accepting one's own mistake or carelessness.

phrases.example: 제 불찰로 인해 불편을 드려서 죄송해요.
phrases.en: I'm sorry for the inconvenience caused by my carelessness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사과할 때 원인을 정중하게 밝히는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to state the cause when apologizing.

phrases.example: 담당자가 이번 일의 불찰에 대해 사과했어요.
phrases.en: The person in charge apologized for their negligence in this matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식 발표나 편지처럼 격식 있는 사과에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits formal apologies such as announcements or letters.

explain_en: It is used to politely admit your own mistake or lack of care, as in '제 불찰이에요' or '저의 불찰입니다'. It is normally about your own fault, and saying '네 불찰이야' to someone else sounds cold. It is more formal than '실수', so it appears often in apologies and official statements.

examples.ko: 말끝마다 시비조로 말하는 사람과는 대화하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: It is hard to talk with someone who picks a fight in every sentence.

examples.ko: 그의 시비조 말투에 기분이 확 나빠졌어요.
examples.en: His confrontational way of speaking really put me in a bad mood.
Why do you keep picking a fight with me?

examples.ko: 손님이 시비조로 따지는 바람에 직원이 당황했어요.
examples.en: The customer argued in a belligerent tone, and the staff member was flustered.
Even to the hostile question, the teacher answered calmly.

examples.ko: 요즘 형은 시비조여서 말 붙이기 어려워요.
examples.en: My brother has been so combative lately that it is hard to talk to him.

explain: '시비를 걸다'처럼 싸움을 걸듯이 따지고 드는 말투나 태도를 말해요. 보통 '시비조로 말하다', '시비조의 말투'처럼 써요. 말하는 방식을 나쁘게 평가할 때 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 그는 늘 시비조로 말해서 사람들이 피해요.
phrases.en: He always talks in a confrontational way, so people avoid him.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시비조'를 가장 기본적으로 쓰는 꼴이에요. 말하는 방식을 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to use 시비조; used to criticize someone's way of speaking.
phrases.en_equiv: to speak in a confrontational tone

phrases.en: I was misunderstood because of my confrontational way of speaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '말투' 앞에 붙여서 싸움을 거는 듯한 말씨를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before 말투 (way of speaking) to describe a speaking style that sounds like picking a fight.

phrases.en: Please don't ask me why I did it in such an aggressive tone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질문하는 태도가 따지는 것처럼 공격적일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the way of asking a question sounds aggressive, as if demanding an answer.
phrases.en_equiv: to ask in an aggressive tone

explain_en: It describes a tone or attitude that sounds like picking a fight, like '시비를 걸다'. It is usually used as '시비조로 말하다' or '시비조의 말투'. It is a negative judgment about the way someone speaks.

examples.ko: 직원이 친절히 알려 줘서 길을 쉽게 찾았어요.
examples.en: The staff member kindly told me, so I found the way easily.

examples.ko: 선생님은 제 질문에 친절히 대답해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher kindly answered my question.
You should treat even strangers kindly.
I kindly gave up my seat to the grandmother.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 약 먹는 법을 친절히 설명해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor kindly explained how to take the medicine.

examples.ko: 손님을 친절히 맞이하는 가게가 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: Shops that welcome customers kindly are popular.

explain: '친절하다'에서 나온 부사예요. '친절하게'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, '친절히'는 조금 글 같은 느낌이 나요. 같은 방식으로 '조용하다'는 '조용히'가 돼요.

phrases.en: The staff member helped me kindly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '친절히'와 거의 같고, 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as '친절히' but more common in speech.

phrases.en: The owner of this shop is really kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 가게가 어떤지 말하는 해요체 형용사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite adjective form describing a person or shop.

phrases.en: Thanks to the kind staff, I felt good.

explain_en: It is the adverb from '친절하다' and means almost the same as '친절하게', though '친절히' sounds a little more written. The same pattern turns '조용하다' into '조용히'.
